sentences.zh: 列傳第一百三十一史憲誠史憲誠，其先出於奚虜，今爲靈武建康人。

translations.literal: Biography 131: Shi Xiancheng. Shi Xiancheng's ancestors came from the Xi people; he was now registered as a native of Jiankang in Lingwu.
translations.idiomatic: Biography 131 — Shi Xiancheng. His forebears were Xi tribesmen; by his day his household was counted among the people of Jiankang in Lingwu.

sentences.zh: 祖道德，開府儀同三司、試太常卿、上柱國、懷澤郡王。

translations.literal: His grandfather Daode held the titles Grand Preceptor of the Palace with Honorary Rank Equal to the Three Excellencies, Acting Grand Master of Ceremonies, Senior Pillar of State, and Prince of Huaize commandery.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Daode was Grand Preceptor of the Palace with the honorary rank equal to the Three Excellencies, acting Grand Master of Ceremonies, Senior Pillar of State, and Prince of Huaize commandery.

sentences.zh: 父周洛，爲魏博軍校，事田季安，至兵馬大使、銀青光祿大夫、檢校太子賓客、兼御史中丞、柱國、北海郡王。

translations.literal: His father Zhouluo served as a military officer in Weibo, attending Tian Ji'an, and rose to Military Commissioner, Silver-Green-Light Grandee, Honorary Crown Prince's Guest, Concurrent Censor-in-Chief, Pillar of State, and Prince of Beihai commandery.
translations.idiomatic: His father Zhouluo was an officer in the Weibo army under Tian Ji'an, rising to Military Commissioner, Silver-Green-Light Grandee, honorary Crown Prince's Guest, concurrent Censor-in-Chief, Pillar of State, and Prince of Beihai commandery.

sentences.zh: 憲誠始以材勇，隨父歷軍中右職，兼監察御史。

translations.literal: Xiancheng began with talent and courage; he followed his father through senior posts in the army and concurrently served as Supervising Censor.
translations.idiomatic: Xiancheng first distinguished himself by ability and valor; he followed his father through senior army posts and also held the post of Supervising Censor.

sentences.zh: 元和中，田弘正討李師道，令憲誠以先鋒四千人濟河，累下其城柵。

translations.literal: In the Yuanhe era Tian Hongzheng campaigned against Li Shidao and ordered Xiancheng to lead four thousand vanguard troops across the Yellow River; he repeatedly captured enemy fortifications.
translations.idiomatic: During the Yuanhe period Tian Hongzheng attacked Li Shidao and sent Xiancheng with four thousand vanguard troops across the Yellow River; he took one enemy strongpoint after another.

sentences.zh: 復以大軍齊進，乘勢逐北，魏之全師迫於鄆之城下。

translations.literal: Then with the main army advancing together they seized the momentum to pursue north; the entire Wei force pressed to below the walls of Yan prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: The main army then advanced in concert, pressing the pursuit northward until the whole Wei host stood beneath the walls of Yan.

sentences.zh: 師道窮蹙，劉悟斬首投魏軍。

translations.literal: Shidao was driven to desperation; Liu Wu beheaded him and surrendered the head to the Wei army.
translations.idiomatic: Shidao was cornered; Liu Wu cut off his head and presented it to the Wei army.

sentences.zh: 錄功，超授憲誠兼中丞。

translations.literal: Recording his merit, Xiancheng was given an extraordinary promotion to Concurrent Censor-in-Chief.
translations.idiomatic: His achievements were entered on the rolls and Xiancheng was promoted out of turn to concurrent Censor-in-Chief.

sentences.zh: 鎮州王承宗死，弘正自魏移領鎮州。

translations.literal: Wang Chengzong of Zhen prefecture died; Hongzheng moved from Wei to take charge of Zhen prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Chengzong of Zhenzhou died, and Hongzheng transferred from Wei to take command of Zhenzhou.

sentences.zh: 居數月，爲王廷湊所殺，遂以兵叛。

translations.literal: After several months he was killed by Wang Tingcou, who then took up arms in rebellion.
translations.idiomatic: Within a few months he was murdered by Wang Tingcou, who then rose in armed rebellion.

sentences.zh: 朝廷以弘正子布爲魏博節度使，領兵討伐，俾復父冤。

translations.literal: The court appointed Hongzheng's son Bu military commissioner of Weibo and ordered troops to campaign so that he might avenge his father.
translations.idiomatic: The court made Hongzheng's son Bu military commissioner of Weibo and sent him to campaign, that he might avenge his father.

sentences.zh: 時幽州硃克融援助廷湊，布不能制，因自引決，軍情囂然。

translations.literal: At that time Zhu Kerong of You prefecture aided Tingcou; Bu could not control the situation and took his own life; army morale grew turbulent.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Kerong of Youzhou then aided Tingcou; Bu could not master the situation and took his own life, and the army's temper grew unruly.

sentences.zh: 憲誠爲中軍都知兵馬使，乘亂以河朔舊事動其人心，諸軍即擁而歸魏，共立爲帥，國家因而命之。

translations.literal: Xiancheng was Commander of the Central Army in charge of military affairs; amid the turmoil he stirred hearts with old Hebei precedents; the troops at once rallied to him and returned to Wei, jointly establishing him as commander; the state thereupon confirmed his appointment.
translations.idiomatic: Xiancheng was commander of the central army in charge of military affairs; seizing the disorder, he stirred the men with old Hebei precedents, and the armies at once rallied to him and returned to Wei, jointly setting him up as commander — whereupon the court confirmed him in office.

sentences.zh: 時克融、廷湊並據兵爲亂，憲誠喜得旄節，雖外順朝旨，而中與硃、王爲輔車之勢，長慶二年正月也。

translations.literal: At that time Kerong and Tingcou both held armies in rebellion; Xiancheng was delighted to receive the commission and military insignia; though outwardly compliant with court orders, inwardly he formed with Zhu and Wang a relationship of mutual support — in the first month of the second year of Changqing.
translations.idiomatic: Kerong and Tingcou both held troops in rebellion at the time; Xiancheng rejoiced to receive the commission and insignia; though outwardly he obeyed the court, inwardly he and Zhu and Wang stood in mutual support — this was in the first month of Changqing year 2.

sentences.zh: 尋遣司門郎中韋文恪宣慰。

translations.literal: Soon thereafter the court sent Wei Wenke of the Ministry of Rites, Department of Credentials, as emissary to console and reassure.
translations.idiomatic: Soon the court sent Wei Wenke, a director in the Ministry of Rites' Department of Credentials, to offer consolation and reassurance.

sentences.zh: 時李㝏爲亂，與憲誠書問交通。

translations.literal: At that time Li Tongjie was in rebellion and exchanged letters with Xiancheng.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Li Tongjie was in rebellion and exchanged messages with Xiancheng.

sentences.zh: 憲誠表請與㝏節鉞，仍於黎陽艤舟，示欲渡河。

translations.literal: Xiancheng memorialized requesting that he and Tongjie each receive military commissions, and moreover anchored boats at Liyang, showing intent to cross the river.
translations.idiomatic: Xiancheng memorialized asking that he and Tongjie each receive military commissions, and moreover moored boats at Liyang as if preparing to cross the river.

sentences.zh: 及見文恪，舉止驕倨，其言甚悖。

translations.literal: When he met Wenke his conduct was arrogant and his words greatly insubordinate.
translations.idiomatic: When he met Wenke his bearing was proud and his words deeply insubordinate.

sentences.zh: 旋聞絺爲帳下所殺，乃從改過，謂文恪曰：「憲誠蕃人，猶狗也，唯能識主。

translations.literal: Soon he heard that Li Ge had been killed by his own subordinates; he then changed his tone, saying to Wenke: "Xiancheng is a barbarian, like a dog — he knows only his master."
translations.idiomatic: Before long he heard that Li Ge had been killed by his own tent guards; he then changed his manner and told Wenke, "Xiancheng is a barbarian, no better than a dog — he knows only to recognize his master."

sentences.zh: 雖被棒打，終不忍離。

translations.literal: "Though beaten with a stick, he could not bear to leave."
translations.idiomatic: "Even when beaten with a stick, he cannot bear to leave his master."

sentences.zh: 」其狡譎如此。

translations.literal: Such was his cunning and deceit.
translations.idiomatic: Such was the depth of his cunning.

sentences.zh: 朝廷每爲優容，尋加左僕射。

translations.literal: The court repeatedly showed him forbearance; he was soon promoted to Left Vice Minister of Works.
translations.idiomatic: The court repeatedly indulged him; he was soon made Left Vice Minister of Works.

sentences.zh: 敬宗即位，進秩司空。

translations.literal: When Emperor Jingzong ascended the throne, Xiancheng advanced to Grand Minister of Works.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Jingzong took the throne, Xiancheng was promoted to Grand Minister of Works.

sentences.zh: 太和二年，滄景節度使李全略卒，其子同捷竊據軍城，表邀符節，舉兵伐之。

translations.literal: In the second year of Taihe, Li Quanlue, military commissioner of Cangjing, died; his son Tongjie seized the garrison and petitioned for the commission and insignia; Xiancheng raised troops to attack him.
translations.idiomatic: In Taihe year 2 Li Quanlue, military commissioner of Cangjing, died; his son Tongjie seized the garrison and petitioned for the commission and insignia, and Xiancheng raised troops to attack him.

sentences.zh: 先是，憲誠與全略婚媾，及同捷叛，復潛以糧餉爲助。

translations.literal: Earlier Xiancheng had been allied by marriage with Quanlue; when Tongjie rebelled he again secretly supplied grain and provisions as aid.
translations.idiomatic: Xiancheng had earlier been joined to Quanlue by marriage; when Tongjie rebelled he again secretly sent grain and supplies as aid.

sentences.zh: 上屢發使申諭，尋又就加平章事。

translations.literal: The emperor repeatedly sent envoys to admonish him; he was then given the additional title of Grand Councilor.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor repeatedly sent envoys to instruct him; he was then given the additional title of Grand Councilor.

sentences.zh: 憲誠嘗遣驍將至闕下，恣爲張大，宰相韋處厚以語折剉之，憲誠不敢復與同捷爲應。

translations.literal: Xiancheng had once sent fierce generals to the capital to boast extravagantly; Grand Councilor Wei Chuhou rebuked him with pointed words; Xiancheng dared not again coordinate with Tongjie.
translations.idiomatic: Xiancheng had once sent fierce generals to the capital to swagger and boast; the chief minister Wei Chuhou cut him down with sharp words, and Xiancheng dared not again act in concert with Tongjie.

sentences.zh: 時憲誠示出師共討同捷。

translations.literal: At that time Xiancheng feigned dispatching troops to join in attacking Tongjie jointly.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Xiancheng made a show of marching out to join in the campaign against Tongjie.

sentences.zh: 及滄景平，加司徒。

translations.literal: When Cangjing was pacified he was promoted to Grand Mentor of State.
translations.idiomatic: When Cangjing was pacified, he was made Grand Mentor of State.

sentences.zh: 憲誠心不自安，乃遣子孝章入覲，又飛章願以所管奉命。

translations.literal: Xiancheng's heart was ill at ease; he sent his son Xiaozhang to court for audience and also sent urgent memorials offering to place his jurisdiction under court command.
translations.idiomatic: Xiancheng felt ill at ease in his heart; he sent his son Xiaozhang to court for audience and also sent urgent memorials offering to place his command under the court's orders.

sentences.zh: 上嘉之。

translations.literal: The emperor praised this.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor commended this.

sentences.zh: 乃加侍中，移鎮河中。

translations.literal: He was then made Palace Attendant and transferred to garrison at Hezhong.
translations.idiomatic: He was then made Palace Attendant and transferred to command at Hezhong.

sentences.zh: 憲誠素懷向背，不能以忠誠感激其眾。

translations.literal: Xiancheng had long harbored divided loyalties and could not inspire his men with steadfast devotion.
translations.idiomatic: Xiancheng had long wavered in loyalty and could not move his men with sincere devotion.

sentences.zh: 未及出城，太和三年六月二十六日夜，爲軍眾所害，冊贈太尉。

translations.literal: Before he had left the city, on the night of the twenty-sixth day of the sixth month of the third year of Taihe, he was killed by the troops; posthumously enfeoffed as Grand Preceptor of State.
translations.idiomatic: Before he had even left the city, on the night of the twenty-sixth day of the sixth month of Taihe year 3, the troops killed him; he was posthumously enfeoffed as Grand Preceptor of State.

sentences.zh: 憲誠子 孝章孝章，幼聰悟好學。

translations.literal: Xiancheng's son Xiaozhang. Xiaozhang was clever and fond of learning from childhood.
translations.idiomatic: Xiancheng's son Xiaozhang. Xiaozhang was clever and fond of study from boyhood.

sentences.zh: 元和中，李醞爲魏帥，取大將子弟列於軍籍。

translations.literal: In the Yuanhe era when Li Yun was military commander of Wei he enrolled the sons of senior generals on the military rolls.
translations.idiomatic: In the Yuanhe era, when Li Yun was military commissioner of Wei, he enrolled the sons of senior generals on the army rolls.

sentences.zh: 孝章倡言願效文職，醞奇之，令攝府參軍。

translations.literal: Xiaozhang stepped forward saying he wished to serve in a civil post; Yun was struck by this and had him act as adjutant to the headquarters.
translations.idiomatic: Xiaozhang spoke up saying he wished to serve in a civil post; Yun was impressed and had him serve as acting headquarters adjutant.

sentences.zh: 及憲誠領節鉞，改士曹參軍、兼監察御史，賜緋。

translations.literal: When Xiancheng received the military commission, Xiaozhang was changed to Registrar of the Bureau of Personnel Affairs and concurrently Supervising Censor; he was granted crimson official dress.
translations.idiomatic: When Xiancheng received the military commission, Xiaozhang was made registrar in the Bureau of Personnel and concurrent Supervising Censor, and was granted crimson robes.

sentences.zh: 孝章以父在鎮多違朝旨，嘗雪涕極諫，備陳逆順之理。

translations.literal: Xiaozhang, because his father in his command often violated court orders, once wept blood and remonstrated to the limit, fully expounding the principles of loyalty and rebellion.
translations.idiomatic: Because his father in his command often defied the court, Xiaozhang once wept as he remonstrated to the utmost, setting forth in full the logic of loyalty and rebellion.

sentences.zh: 朝廷聞而嘉之，乃授檢校太子左諭德、兼侍御史，充節度副使。

translations.literal: When the court heard of this it commended him; he was appointed Honorary Mentor of the Left to the Crown Prince and Concurrent Attending Censor, and made deputy military commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: The court heard of this and commended him; he was appointed honorary Left Mentor to the Crown Prince and concurrent Attending Censor, and made deputy military commissioner.

sentences.zh: 累遷至散騎常侍、兼御史大夫，賜紫。

translations.literal: He was promoted repeatedly to Regular Attendant and Concurrent Censor-in-Chief, and granted purple official dress.
translations.idiomatic: He rose in stages to Regular Attendant and concurrent Censor-in-Chief, and was granted purple robes.

sentences.zh: 領本道兵同平滄景，加工部尚書。

translations.literal: Leading troops of his circuit he helped pacify Cangjing, and was given the additional post of Minister of Revenue.
translations.idiomatic: Leading troops of his circuit he helped pacify Cangjing and was given the additional post of Minister of Revenue.

sentences.zh: 尋請赴闕，文宗慰勞甚厚，憲誠亦因懇乞朝覲。

translations.literal: Soon he requested to go to court; Emperor Wenzong comforted and rewarded him generously; Xiancheng also because of this earnestly begged to attend court.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he asked to go to court; Emperor Wenzong comforted and rewarded him generously, and Xiancheng also earnestly begged to attend court because of this.

sentences.zh: 上知憲誠之入覲，自孝章之謀，遂加禮部尚書，分相、衞、澶三州別爲一鎮，俾孝章領之。

translations.literal: The emperor knew Xiancheng's coming to court was due to Xiaozhang's counsel; he then promoted Xiaozhang to Minister of Rites, and separated Xiang, Wei, and Chan prefectures into a distinct command so Xiaozhang could govern it.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor knew Xiancheng's coming to court sprang from Xiaozhang's counsel; he then promoted Xiaozhang to Minister of Rites and carved Xiang, Wei, and Chan into a separate command for Xiaozhang to govern.

sentences.zh: 孝章未到鎮，憲誠遇害。

translations.literal: Before Xiaozhang reached his post, Xiancheng met with disaster.
translations.idiomatic: Before Xiaozhang reached his post, Xiancheng was killed.

sentences.zh: 上以孝章有忠節，起復爲右金吾衞將軍。

translations.literal: Because the emperor considered Xiaozhang loyal, he was recalled from mourning to serve as General of the Right Imperial Insignia Guard.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor, considering Xiaozhang loyal, recalled him from mourning to serve as general of the Right Imperial Insignia Guard.

sentences.zh: 間歲，授鄜坊節度使。

translations.literal: After a year he was appointed military commissioner of Bin and Fang.
translations.idiomatic: A year later he was appointed military commissioner of Bin and Fang.

sentences.zh: 居四年，遷於滑。

translations.literal: After four years he was transferred to Hua.
translations.idiomatic: After four years in office he was transferred to command Hua.

sentences.zh: 一歲，入爲右領軍大將軍，改右金吾大將軍，俄授邠寧節度。

translations.literal: One year later he entered court as Grand General of the Right Army; he was changed to Grand General of the Right Imperial Insignia Guard; shortly thereafter he was given the Binning command.
translations.idiomatic: One year later he entered court as grand general of the Right Army, then was changed to grand general of the Right Imperial Insignia Guard, and soon received the Binning command.

sentences.zh: 孝章歷三鎮，雖無異績，而謹身畏法，以保初終。

translations.literal: Xiaozhang held three commands; though without outstanding achievement, he guarded himself with fear of law and preserved his beginning and end.
translations.idiomatic: Xiaozhang held three commands; though he achieved nothing remarkable, he kept himself within the law and preserved his position from first to last.

sentences.zh: 開成三年十月卒，贈右僕射。

translations.literal: In the tenth month of the third year of Kaicheng he died; posthumously enfeoffed as Right Vice Minister of Works.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month of Kaicheng year 3 he died and was posthumously enfeoffed as Right Vice Minister of Works.

sentences.zh: 何進滔何進滔，靈武人也。

translations.literal: He Jintao. He Jintao was a native of Lingwu.
translations.idiomatic: He Jintao. He Jintao was a man of Lingwu.

sentences.zh: 曾祖孝物，祖俊，並本州軍校。

translations.literal: His great-grandfather Xiaowu and grandfather Jun were both military officers of the prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: His great-grandfather Xiaowu and grandfather Jun had both been military officers of the prefecture.

sentences.zh: 父默，夏州衙前兵馬使，檢校太子賓客，試太常卿。

translations.literal: His father Mo was Military Commissioner in the Yamen of Xia prefecture, Honorary Crown Prince's Guest, Acting Grand Master of Ceremonies.
translations.idiomatic: His father Mo was military commissioner in the yamen of Xia prefecture, honorary Crown Prince's Guest, and acting Grand Master of Ceremonies.

sentences.zh: 以進滔之貴，贈左散騎常侍。

translations.literal: Because of Jintao's eminence, Mo was posthumously given the title of Left Regular Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: When Jintao rose to eminence, Mo was posthumously given Left Regular Attendant.

sentences.zh: 進滔客寄於魏，委質軍門，事節度使田弘正。

translations.literal: Jintao lived as a guest in Wei and pledged himself to the military gate, serving military commissioner Tian Hongzheng.
translations.idiomatic: Jintao lodged in Wei and pledged himself at the military gate, serving the military commissioner Tian Hongzheng.

sentences.zh: 弘正奉詔討鄆州，破李師道，時進滔爲衙內都知兵馬使，以功授兼侍御史。

translations.literal: Hongzheng carried out an imperial order to attack Yan prefecture and defeat Li Shidao; at that time Jintao was Commander of the Inner Yamen in charge of military affairs; for his merit he was given the additional post of Attending Censor.
translations.idiomatic: Hongzheng carried out the imperial order to attack Yanzhou and defeat Li Shidao; at that time Jintao was commander of the inner yamen in charge of military affairs, and for his merit was given the additional post of Attending Censor.

sentences.zh: 太和三年，軍眾害史憲誠，連聲而呼曰：「得衙內都知兵馬使何端公知留後，即三軍安矣。

translations.literal: In the third year of Taihe the army killed Shi Xiancheng; they shouted in unison: "If we get the Commander of the Inner Yamen, Master He Duke, to know affairs as acting commander, the three armies will be at peace!"
translations.idiomatic: In Taihe year 3 the troops killed Shi Xiancheng; they shouted together, "If the commander of the inner yamen, Master He the Duke, will act as acting commander, the three armies will be secure!"

sentences.zh: 」推而立之。

translations.literal: They pushed him forward and established him.
translations.idiomatic: They pushed him forward and set him up.

sentences.zh: 朝廷因授進滔左散騎常侍、魏博等州節度觀察處置等使。

translations.literal: The court thereupon appointed Jintao Left Regular Attendant and Military Commissioner of Weibo and other prefectures, with authority to observe and dispose.
translations.idiomatic: The court thereupon appointed Jintao Left Regular Attendant and military commissioner of Weibo and other prefectures, with authority to observe and dispose.

sentences.zh: 爲魏帥十餘年，大得民情，累官至司徒、平章事卒。

translations.literal: As military commander of Wei for more than ten years he won the hearts of the people greatly; he rose in rank repeatedly to Grand Mentor of State and Grand Councilor and died.
translations.idiomatic: As commander of Wei for more than ten years he won the people's hearts; he rose in rank to Grand Mentor of State and Grand Councilor and died.

sentences.zh: 進滔子 弘敬子弘敬襲其位。

translations.literal: Jintao's son Hongjing — Hongjing inherited his position.
translations.idiomatic: Jintao's son Hongjing. Hongjing inherited his position.

sentences.zh: 朝廷時遣河中帥李執方、滄州帥劉約各遣使勸令歸闕，別俟朝旨。

translations.literal: The court at that time sent Li Zhifang military commander of Hezhong and Liu Yue military commander of Cangzhou, each dispatching envoys to urge him to return to court and await further imperial orders separately.
translations.idiomatic: The court at that time sent Li Zhifang, commander of Hezhong, and Liu Yue, commander of Cangzhou, each to dispatch envoys urging him to return to court and await separate imperial orders.

sentences.zh: 弘敬不從，竟就加節制。

translations.literal: Hongjing did not comply and nevertheless received the commission and military control directly.
translations.idiomatic: Hongjing did not comply and nevertheless received the commission and military control outright.

sentences.zh: 及劉稹反，不時起兵。

translations.literal: When Liu Zhen rebelled, he did not raise troops promptly.
translations.idiomatic: When Liu Zhen rebelled he did not raise troops promptly.

sentences.zh: 鎮州王元逵下邢、洺二州，兵次上黨，弘敬方出師壓境。

translations.literal: Wang Yuankui of Zhen prefecture took Xing and Ming prefectures; his troops reached Shangdang; only then did Hongjing march out to press the border.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Yuankui of Zhenzhou took Xing and Ming prefectures and advanced to Shangdang; only then did Hongjing march out to press the border.

sentences.zh: 大中後，宣宗務其姑息，繼加官爵，亦至使相。

translations.literal: After the Dazhong era, Emperor Xuanzong pursued appeasement; he successively added offices and enfeoffments until Hongjing too reached the rank of commissioner and councilor.
translations.idiomatic: After the Dazhong era Emperor Xuanzong pursued appeasement and piled offices and enfeoffments upon him until Hongjing too reached commissioner and councilor.

sentences.zh: 咸通初，卒。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Xiantong he died.
translations.idiomatic: He died early in the Xiantong era.

sentences.zh: 子全皞嗣之。

translations.literal: His son Quanhao succeeded him.
translations.idiomatic: His son Quanhao succeeded to his post.

sentences.zh: 朝廷尋降符節，累官亦至同平章事。

translations.literal: The court soon bestowed the commission and insignia; he too rose in office to Concurrent Grand Councilor.
translations.idiomatic: The court soon bestowed the commission and insignia; he too rose to concurrent Grand Councilor.

sentences.zh: 十一年，爲軍人所害。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year he was killed by the troops.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh year the troops killed him.

sentences.zh: 子孫相繼，四十餘年。

translations.literal: Father and son succeeded one another for more than forty years.
translations.idiomatic: Father and son held power in succession for more than forty years.

sentences.zh: 韓允忠韓允忠，魏州人也。

translations.literal: Han Yunzhong. Han Yunzhong was a native of Weizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Han Yunzhong. Han Yunzhong was a man of Weizhou.

sentences.zh: 舊名君雄，懿宗改賜今名。

translations.literal: His original name was Junxiong; Emperor Yizong changed and bestowed the present name.
translations.idiomatic: His original name was Junxiong; Emperor Yizong changed it and bestowed the present name.

sentences.zh: 父國昌，歷本州右職。

translations.literal: His father Guochang held right-hand posts in the prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: His father Guochang held senior posts on the right in the prefecture.

sentences.zh: 會昌中，從何弘敬破劉稹，以功爲貝州刺史、兼御史中丞。

translations.literal: In the Huichang era he followed He Hongjing in defeating Liu Zhen; for merit he was made Prefect of Bei prefecture and Concurrent Censor-in-Chief.
translations.idiomatic: In the Huichang era he followed He Hongjing in defeating Liu Zhen; for merit he was made prefect of Bei prefecture and concurrent Censor-in-Chief.

sentences.zh: 以允忠故，累贈兵部尚書。

translations.literal: Because of Yunzhong, Guochang was repeatedly promoted posthumously to Minister of War.
translations.idiomatic: Because of Yunzhong, Guochang was repeatedly promoted posthumously to Minister of War.

sentences.zh: 允忠少仕軍門，繼升裨校。

translations.literal: Yunzhong entered military service young and rose stepwise to staff officer.
translations.idiomatic: Yunzhong entered military service young and rose step by step to staff officer.

sentences.zh: 潞州之役，亦與其行。

translations.literal: In the campaign at Lu prefecture he also marched with them.
translations.idiomatic: In the Lu prefecture campaign he marched with them as well.

sentences.zh: 咸通十一年，何全皞爲軍眾所殺，推允忠爲帥。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year of Xiantong, when He Quanhao was killed by the troops, they pushed Yunzhong forward as commander.
translations.idiomatic: In Xiantong year 11, when He Quanhao was killed by the troops, they pushed Yunzhong forward as commander.

sentences.zh: 時僖宗爲普王，即降詔遙領節度，授允忠左散騎常侍、兼御史中丞，充節度觀察留後。

translations.literal: At that time Emperor Xizong was Prince of Pu; an edict was promptly issued putting him in charge of the command remotely; Yunzhong was given Left Regular Attendant and Concurrent Censor-in-Chief, acting Military Commissioner in Observation, as acting commander.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Emperor Xizong was Prince of Pu; an edict was promptly issued putting him in remote charge of the command; Yunzhong was given Left Regular Attendant and concurrent Censor-in-Chief as acting military commissioner in observation.

sentences.zh: 不數月，轉檢校工部尚書、魏州大都督府長史、充魏博節度觀察等使。

translations.literal: Within a few months he was changed to Honorary Minister of Works, Chief Administrator of the Great Capital Prefecture of Weizhou, and full Military Commissioner of Weibo in observation, etc.
translations.idiomatic: Within a few months he was made honorary Minister of Works, chief administrator of the great capital prefecture of Weizhou, and full military commissioner of Weibo in observation, and so on.

sentences.zh: 累加至檢校司空、同平章事。

translations.literal: He was promoted repeatedly to Honorary Grand Minister of Works and Concurrent Grand Councilor.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted repeatedly to honorary Grand Minister of Works and concurrent Grand Councilor.

sentences.zh: 乾符元年十一月卒，年六十一。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month of the first year of Qianfu he died, age sixty-one.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month of Qianfu year 1 he died, aged sixty-one.

sentences.zh: 累贈太尉。

translations.literal: He was repeatedly enfeoffed posthumously as Grand Preceptor of State.
translations.idiomatic: Posthumously he was repeatedly enfeoffed as Grand Preceptor of State.

sentences.zh: 允忠子 簡子簡，自允忠初授戎帥，便爲節度副使。

translations.literal: Yunzhong's son Jian — Jian, from the time Yunzhong first received the military command, served as deputy military commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: Yunzhong's son Jian. Jian, from the time Yunzhong first received the military command, served as deputy military commissioner.

sentences.zh: 乾符初，累官至檢校工部尚書。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Qianfu he had risen in office repeatedly to Honorary Minister of Works.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Qianfu he had risen repeatedly to honorary Minister of Works.

sentences.zh: 允忠卒，即起復爲節度觀察留後。

translations.literal: When Yunzhong died he was recalled from mourning to serve as acting Military Commissioner in observation.
translations.idiomatic: When Yunzhong died he was recalled from mourning to serve as acting military commissioner in observation.

sentences.zh: 逾月，加檢校右僕射。

translations.literal: After more than a month he was given the additional title of Honorary Right Vice Minister of Works.
translations.idiomatic: After more than a month he was given the additional title of honorary Right Vice Minister of Works.

sentences.zh: 其後累加至侍中，封昌黎郡王。

translations.literal: Thereafter he was promoted repeatedly to Palace Attendant and enfeoffed as Prince of Changli commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Later he rose to Palace Attendant and was enfeoffed Prince of Changli commandery.

sentences.zh: 賊巢之亂，諸葛爽受其偽命河陽節度使。

translations.literal: During the disorder of Huang Chao's bandits, Zhuge Shuang received the false appointment as military commissioner of Heyang.
translations.idiomatic: During the upheaval of Huang Chao's rebels, Zhuge Shuang received the false appointment as military commissioner of Heyang.

sentences.zh: 時僖宗在蜀，寇盜蜂起，簡據有六州，甲兵強盛，竊懷僭亂之志，且欲啟其封疆，乃舉兵攻河陽，爽棄城而走。

translations.literal: At that time Emperor Xizong was in Shu; bandits and marauders swarmed; Jian held six prefectures with strong armor and troops, secretly harbored ambitions of usurpation and moreover wished to expand his territory; he raised troops to attack Heyang; Shuang abandoned the city and fled.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Emperor Xizong was in Shu and bandits swarmed everywhere; Jian held six prefectures with strong armor and troops, secretly harbored ambitions of usurpation, and wished besides to enlarge his domain; he raised troops to attack Heyang, and Shuang abandoned the city and fled.

sentences.zh: 簡遂留兵保守，因北掠邢、洺而歸，遂移軍攻鄆。

translations.literal: Jian left troops to hold it, then raided north into Xing and Ming and returned, then shifted his army to attack Yan.
translations.idiomatic: Jian left troops to hold it, then raided north through Xing and Ming and returned, then shifted his army to attack Yan.

sentences.zh: 鄆帥曹全晸出戰，爲簡所敗，死之。

translations.literal: Cao Quanzhen military commander of Yan went out to battle and was defeated by Jian and killed.
translations.idiomatic: Cao Quanzhen, military commissioner of Yan, went out to fight, was defeated by Jian, and was killed.

sentences.zh: 鄆將崔君裕收合殘眾，保鄆州。

translations.literal: Yan general Cui Junyu gathered the remnant forces and held Yan prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: The Yan general Cui Junyu gathered the remnant forces and held Yan prefecture.

sentences.zh: 簡進攻其城，半年不下，河陽復爲諸葛爽所襲。

translations.literal: Jian pressed the attack on the city for half a year without taking it; Heyang was again seized by Shuang in a raid.
translations.idiomatic: Jian pressed the attack on the city for half a year without taking it; Heyang was again seized in a raid by Shuang.

sentences.zh: 簡因欲先討君裕，次及河陽，乃舉兵至鄆，君裕請降。

translations.literal: Jian therefore wished first to subdue Junyu, then turn to Heyang; he raised troops to Yan; Junyu requested surrender.
translations.idiomatic: Jian therefore wished first to subdue Junyu and then turn to Heyang; he raised troops to Yan and Junyu asked to surrender.

sentences.zh: 尋移軍復攻河陽，行及新鄕，爲爽軍逆擊，敗之。

translations.literal: Soon he shifted troops again to attack Heyang; marching to Xinxiang he was met and struck by Shuang's army and defeated.
translations.idiomatic: He soon shifted troops to attack Heyang again; at Xinxiang he was met by Shuang's army, struck, and defeated.

sentences.zh: 簡單騎奔回，憂憤。

translations.literal: Jian fled back alone on horseback, troubled and resentful.
translations.idiomatic: Jian fled back alone on horseback, full of grief and resentment.

sentences.zh: 疽發背而卒，時中和元年十一月也。

translations.literal: A carbuncle broke out on his back and he died — this was the eleventh month of the first year of Zhonghe.
translations.idiomatic: A carbuncle broke out on his back and he died — this was the eleventh month of Zhonghe year 1.

sentences.zh: 樂彥禎樂彥禎，魏州人也。

translations.literal: Li Yanzhen. Li Yanzhen was a native of Weizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Li Yanzhen. Li Yanzhen was a man of Weizhou.

sentences.zh: 父少寂，歷澶、博、貝三州刺史，贈工部尚書。

translations.literal: His father Shaoji had served as prefect of Chan, Bo, and Bei prefectures and was posthumously given the title Minister of Works.
translations.idiomatic: His father Shaoji had served as prefect of Chan, Bo, and Bei prefectures and was posthumously made Minister of Works.

sentences.zh: 彥禎少爲本州軍校。

translations.literal: Yanzhen in youth was a military officer of the prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: In youth Yanzhen was a military officer of the prefecture.

sentences.zh: 韓簡之領節旄也，以彥禎爲馬歩軍都虞候，轉博州刺史。

translations.literal: When Han Jian received the military commission, Yanzhen was made Chief Commandant of the Horse and Foot Army and transferred to Prefect of Bo prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: When Han Jian received the military commission, Yanzhen was made chief commandant of the horse and foot army and then prefect of Bo prefecture.

sentences.zh: 下河陽，走諸葛爽。

translations.literal: He descended on Heyang and drove Zhuge Shuang to flight.
translations.idiomatic: He attacked Heyang and drove Zhuge Shuang to flight.

sentences.zh: 有功，遷澶州刺史。

translations.literal: For merit he was transferred to Prefect of Chan prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: For merit he was transferred to prefect of Chan prefecture.

sentences.zh: 簡再討河陽之敗也。

translations.literal: This was when Jian again campaigned against Heyang and was defeated.
translations.idiomatic: This was when Jian again attacked Heyang and was defeated.

sentences.zh: 彥禎以一軍先歸，魏人遂共立之。

translations.literal: Yanzhen returned first with one army; the people of Wei thereupon jointly established him.
translations.idiomatic: Yanzhen returned first with one army, and the people of Wei thereupon jointly set him up.

sentences.zh: 朝廷尋授檢校工部尚書，知魏博留後。

translations.literal: The court soon appointed him Honorary Minister of Works and acting commander of Weibo.
translations.idiomatic: The court soon appointed him honorary Minister of Works and acting commander of Weibo.

sentences.zh: 俄加戸部尚書，充節度觀察處置等使。

translations.literal: Shortly he was given the additional title of Minister of Revenue and made full Military Commissioner in observation and disposal, etc.
translations.idiomatic: Shortly he was made Minister of Revenue and full military commissioner in observation and disposal, and so on.

sentences.zh: 中和四年，累加至尚書左僕射、同平章事。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Zhonghe he was promoted repeatedly to Left Vice Minister of Works and Concurrent Grand Councilor.
translations.idiomatic: In Zhonghe year 4 he was promoted repeatedly to Left Vice Minister of Works and concurrent Grand Councilor.

sentences.zh: 僖宗自蜀回，加開府儀同三司，冊拜司徒。

translations.literal: When Emperor Xizong returned from Shu he was given the additional title Grand Preceptor of the Palace with Honorary Rank Equal to the Three Excellencies and was enfeoffed by edict as Grand Mentor of State.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Xizong returned from Shu he was given Grand Preceptor of the Palace with honorary rank equal to the Three Excellencies and was enfeoffed by edict as Grand Mentor of State.

sentences.zh: 彥禎志滿驕大，動多不法。

translations.literal: Yanzhen's ambition was full and he grew proud and arrogant; his actions were often unlawful.
translations.idiomatic: Yanzhen's heart swelled with pride; his conduct was often unlawful.

sentences.zh: 一旦征六州之眾，板築羅城，約河門舊堤，周八十里，月餘而畢，人用怨咨。

translations.literal: On one occasion he mobilized the masses of the six prefectures to build the outer wall with rammed earth, following the old embankment at Hemen, eighty li in circuit; it was completed in more than a month, and the people murmured in resentment.
translations.idiomatic: Once he mobilized the people of the six prefectures to build the outer wall with rammed earth along the old embankment at Hemen, eighty li around; it was finished in more than a month, and the people groaned in resentment.

sentences.zh: 彥禎子 從訓又其子從訓天資悖逆。

translations.literal: Yanzhen's son Congxun. Moreover his son Congxun was by nature rebellious and perverse.
translations.idiomatic: Yanzhen's son Congxun. His son Congxun was by nature rebellious and perverse.

sentences.zh: 王鐸自滑移鎮滄州，過魏郊，從訓見其女妓，利之，先伏兵於漳南高雞泊，俟鐸之至，圍而害之，掠其所有。

translations.literal: Wang Duo transferred from Hua to command Cangzhou and passed through Wei territory; Congxun saw his daughter's singing girls and coveted them; he first hid troops at Gaojipo south of Zhang; when Duo arrived he surrounded and killed him and plundered all he had.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Duo moved from Hua to command Cangzhou and passed through Wei territory; Congxun saw his daughter's singing girls and coveted them; he first hid troops at Gaojipo south of Zhang, and when Duo arrived he surrounded and killed him and plundered everything he had.

sentences.zh: 時朝廷微弱，不能詰。

translations.literal: At that time the court was weak and could not call him to account.
translations.idiomatic: The court was weak at the time and could not call him to account.

sentences.zh: 魏人素知鐸名望，議者惜之，而罪從訓。

translations.literal: The people of Wei had long known Duo's reputation; commentators regretted this, and blamed Congxun.
translations.idiomatic: The people of Wei had long known Duo's reputation; commentators regretted the affair and blamed Congxun.

sentences.zh: 從訓又召亡命之徒五百餘輩，出入臥內，號爲「子將」，委以腹心。

translations.literal: Congxun also summoned more than five hundred fugitives who came and went within his sleeping quarters; they were called "Junior Generals" and he entrusted them with his innermost confidence.
translations.idiomatic: Congxun also summoned more than five hundred fugitives who came and went within his sleeping quarters; they were called the "Junior Generals," and he entrusted them with his innermost confidence.

sentences.zh: 軍人籍籍，各有異議。

translations.literal: Among the soldiers there was murmuring; each had his own opinion.
translations.idiomatic: The soldiers murmured among themselves; each held his own view.

sentences.zh: 從訓聞而忌之，易服遁出，止於近縣。

translations.literal: Congxun heard of this and grew jealous; he changed clothes and slipped out, staying in a nearby county.
translations.idiomatic: When Congxun heard of this he grew jealous, changed clothes, slipped out, and stayed in a nearby county.

sentences.zh: 彥禎因命爲六州都指揮使。

translations.literal: Yanzhen thereupon appointed him Commander-in-Chief of the Six Prefectures.
translations.idiomatic: Yanzhen thereupon appointed him commander-in-chief of the six prefectures.

sentences.zh: 未幾，又兼相州刺史。

translations.literal: Before long he was also made Concurrent Prefect of Xiang prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he was also made concurrent prefect of Xiang prefecture.

sentences.zh: 到任之後，般輦軍器，取索錢帛，使人來往，交午塗路，軍府疑貳。

translations.literal: After he took office he carted military equipment and extorted money and silk; messengers came and went until the roads crossed like a checkerboard, and the military headquarters grew doubtful and divided.
translations.idiomatic: After taking office he carted arms, extorted money and silk, and sent messengers back and forth until the roads were crowded; the headquarters grew divided.

sentences.zh: 彥禎危憤而卒，眾推都將趙文㺹知留後事。

translations.literal: Yanzhen died in peril and resentment; the masses pushed forward the chief commander Zhao Wenbi to know acting commander affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Yanzhen died in peril and resentment; the masses pushed forward the chief commander Zhao Wenbi to handle acting commander affairs.

sentences.zh: 從訓自相州領兵三萬餘人至城下，文㺹按兵不出。

translations.literal: Congxun led more than thirty thousand men from Xiang prefecture to the foot of the city; Wenbi held his troops and did not come out.
translations.idiomatic: Congxun led more than thirty thousand men from Xiang prefecture to the foot of the city; Wenbi held his troops and would not come out.

sentences.zh: 眾懷疑懼，復害文㺹，推羅弘信爲帥。

translations.literal: The masses were suspicious and afraid; they again killed Wenbi and pushed Luo Hongxin forward as commander.
translations.idiomatic: The men grew fearful; they killed Wenbi again and set up Luo Hongxin as commander.

sentences.zh: 弘信以兵出戰，敗之。

translations.literal: Hongxin took troops out to fight and defeated him.
translations.idiomatic: Hongxin led troops out to fight and routed him.

sentences.zh: 從訓招集餘眾，次於洹水。

translations.literal: Congxun gathered the remnant forces and encamped at Huan River.
translations.idiomatic: Congxun gathered the remnant forces and encamped at the Huan River.

sentences.zh: 弘信遣將程公佐領兵討擊，大敗之，梟從訓首於軍門，時文德元年春也。

translations.literal: Hongxin sent the general Cheng Gongzuo to lead troops in pursuit and attack; he inflicted a great defeat and displayed Congxun's head at the army gate — this was spring of the first year of Wende.
translations.idiomatic: Hongxin sent the general Cheng Gongzuo to lead troops in pursuit and attack; he inflicted a great defeat and displayed Congxun's head at the army gate — this was spring of Wende year 1.

sentences.zh: 羅弘信羅弘信，字德孚，魏州貴鄕人。

translations.literal: Luo Hongxin. Luo Hongxin, courtesy name Defu, was a native of Guixiang in Weizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Luo Hongxin. Luo Hongxin, courtesy name Defu, was a man of Guixiang in Weizhou.

sentences.zh: 曾祖秀，祖珍，父讓，皆爲本州軍校。

translations.literal: His great-grandfather Xiu, grandfather Zhen, and father Rang were all military officers of the prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: His great-grandfather Xiu, grandfather Zhen, and father Rang had all been military officers of the prefecture.

sentences.zh: 弘信少從戎役，歷事節度使韓簡、樂彥禎。

translations.literal: Hongxin in youth followed military service and successively served the military commissioners Han Jian and Li Yanzhen.
translations.idiomatic: Hongxin entered military service young and served the commissioners Han Jian and Li Yanzhen in turn.

sentences.zh: 光啟末，彥禎子從訓忌牙軍，出居於外，軍眾廢彥禎，推趙文㺹權主軍州事。

translations.literal: At the end of Guangqi, Yanzhen's son Congxun feared the yamen army and went to live outside; the troops deposed Yanzhen and pushed Zhao Wenbi to hold military and prefectural affairs in authority.
translations.idiomatic: At the end of Guangqi, Congxun feared the yamen troops and lived outside; the army deposed Yanzhen and put Zhao Wenbi in charge.

sentences.zh: 眾復以爲不便，因推弘信爲帥。

translations.literal: The masses again found this unsatisfactory and therefore pushed Hongxin forward as commander.
translations.idiomatic: The men again found this unsatisfactory and therefore set up Hongxin as commander.

sentences.zh: 先是，有鄰人密謂弘信曰：「某嘗夜遇一白鬚翁，相告雲，君當爲土地主。

translations.literal: Earlier a neighbor had secretly told Hongxin: "I once met a white-bearded old man at night who told me that you are to be lord of this land."
translations.idiomatic: Earlier a neighbor had secretly told Hongxin, "I once met a white-bearded old man at night who told me you are to be lord of this land."

sentences.zh: 如是者再三。

translations.literal: Thus it happened three times.
translations.idiomatic: This happened three times.

sentences.zh: 」弘信竊異之。

translations.literal: Hongxin privately marveled at it.
translations.idiomatic: Hongxin privately wondered at it.

sentences.zh: 及廢文㺹，軍人聚呼曰：「孰願爲節度使者？

translations.literal: When Wenbi was deposed the soldiers gathered and shouted: "Who wishes to be military commissioner?"
translations.idiomatic: When Wenbi was deposed the soldiers gathered and shouted, "Who wishes to be military commissioner?"

sentences.zh: 」弘信即應之曰：「白鬚翁早以命我。

translations.literal: Hongxin at once answered: "The white-bearded old man long ago commanded me."
translations.idiomatic: Hongxin at once answered, "The white-bearded old man long ago commanded me."

sentences.zh: 」眾乃環而視之，曰：「可也。

translations.literal: The masses then surrounded and looked at him, saying: "He will do."
translations.idiomatic: The masses then surrounded and looked at him, saying, "He will do."

sentences.zh: 」由是立之。

translations.literal: Thereby he was established.
translations.idiomatic: On that basis he was established in command.

sentences.zh: 僖宗聞之，文德元年四月，詔加工部尚書，權知節度留後。

translations.literal: When Emperor Xizong heard of it, in the fourth month of the first year of Wende an edict added the title Minister of Works and put him in authority as acting military commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Xizong heard of it, in the fourth month of Wende year 1 an edict added the title Minister of Works and put him in authority as acting military commissioner.

sentences.zh: 七月，復加金紫光祿大夫、檢校尚書右僕射，充魏博節度觀察處置等使。

translations.literal: In the seventh month he was again given Golden-Green-Light Grandee and Honorary Right Vice Minister of Works and made full Military Commissioner of Weibo in observation and disposal, etc.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month he was again given Golden-Green-Light Grandee and honorary Right Vice Minister of Works and made full military commissioner of Weibo in observation and disposal, and so on.

sentences.zh: 龍紀中，加檢校司空、同平章事，封豫章郡公。

translations.literal: In the Longji era he was given Honorary Grand Minister of Works and Concurrent Grand Councilor and enfeoffed as Duke of Yuzhang commandery.
translations.idiomatic: In the Longji era he was given honorary Grand Minister of Works and concurrent Grand Councilor and enfeoffed as Duke of Yuzhang commandery.

sentences.zh: 乾寧中，朱全忠急攻兗鄆，朱瑄求援於太原。

translations.literal: In the Qianning era Zhu Quanzhong pressed the attack on Yan and Yun; Zhu Xuan sought aid from Taiyuan.
translations.idiomatic: During Qianning, Zhu Quanzhong pressed Yan and Yun hard; Zhu Xuan sought help from Taiyuan.

sentences.zh: 太原發軍，假道於魏，令大將李存信屯莘縣。

translations.literal: Taiyuan sent troops, taking passage through Wei, and ordered the great general Li Cunxin to encamp at Shen county.
translations.idiomatic: Taiyuan sent an army through Wei and ordered Li Cunxin to camp at Shen county.

sentences.zh: 存信御軍無法，侵魏之芻牧，弘信不平之。

translations.literal: Cunxin commanded the army without discipline and encroached on Wei's fodder and pastures; Hongxin was displeased.
translations.idiomatic: Cunxin disciplined his troops poorly and seized Wei's fodder and pasture; Hongxin resented it.

sentences.zh: 全忠復遣人謂之曰：「太原志吞河朔，回戈之日，貴道堪憂。

translations.literal: Quanzhong again sent someone to tell him: "Taiyuan intends to swallow Hebei; on the day it turns its spears back, your territory will be in peril."
translations.idiomatic: Quanzhong again sent someone to tell him, "Taiyuan intends to swallow Hebei; on the day it turns its spears back, your territory will be in peril."

sentences.zh: 」弘信乃托好於汴，出師三萬攻存信，敗之。

translations.literal: Hongxin thereupon feigned friendship with Bian and marched out thirty thousand to attack Cunxin and defeated him.
translations.idiomatic: Hongxin then pretended friendship with Bian, marched out thirty thousand men against Cunxin, and defeated him.

sentences.zh: 太原怒，舉兵攻魏，營於觀音門外。

translations.literal: Taiyuan was enraged and raised troops to attack Wei, encamping outside the Guanyin Gate.
translations.idiomatic: Taiyuan was furious, raised troops against Wei, and encamped outside the Guanyin Gate.

sentences.zh: 汴將葛從周援之，屯於洹水。

translations.literal: The Bian general Ge Congzhou came to aid him and encamped at the Huan River.
translations.idiomatic: The Bian general Ge Congzhou came to his aid and camped on the Huan River.

sentences.zh: 李克用子落落時爲鐵林軍使，爲從周所擒，乃退歸。

translations.literal: Li Keyong's son Luoluo was at that time commander of the Iron Forest Army; he was captured by Congzhou and they then withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: Li Keyong's son Luoluo was at that time commander of the Iron Forest Army; Congzhou captured him and they then withdrew.

sentences.zh: 自是太原之師，每歲侵擾相、魏，魏人患之。

translations.literal: From this time forward the Taiyuan army every year raided Xiang and Wei; the people of Wei suffered from it.
translations.idiomatic: From this time forward the Taiyuan army raided Xiang and Wei every year; the people of Wei suffered from it.

sentences.zh: 朱全忠方事兗鄆，懼弘信離貳，每歲時賂遺，必卑辭厚禮答貺。

translations.literal: Zhu Quanzhong was then engaged with Yan and Yun and feared Hongxin would turn aside; every year at the seasons he sent gifts, and Hongxin always answered with humble words and generous courtesy.
translations.idiomatic: Quanzhong was then fighting Yan and Yun and feared Hongxin would turn; every season he sent gifts, and Hongxin always answered with humble, lavish courtesy.

sentences.zh: 全忠對魏使北面拜而受之，曰：「六兄比予倍年已上，兄弟之國，安得以常鄰遇之。

translations.literal: Quanzhong toward envoys from Wei bowed facing north to receive them, saying: "Sixth Elder Brother is more than twice my years; as brother states, how can we be treated as ordinary neighbors?"
translations.idiomatic: Quanzhong toward envoys from Wei bowed facing north to receive them, saying, "Sixth Elder Brother is more than twice my years; as brother states, how can we be treated as ordinary neighbors?"

sentences.zh: 」弘信以爲厚己，亦推心焉。

translations.literal: Hongxin thought this showed him great honor and also gave him his wholehearted trust.
translations.idiomatic: Hongxin took this as deep regard for himself and gave Quanzhong his full trust.

sentences.zh: 弘信累官至檢校太師、守侍中、臨清王。

translations.literal: Hongxin rose in office repeatedly to Honorary Grand Preceptor of State, Defender Palace Attendant, and Prince of Linqing.
translations.idiomatic: Hongxin rose in office repeatedly to honorary Grand Preceptor of State, defender Palace Attendant, and Prince of Linqing.

sentences.zh: 光化元年九月卒，年六十三，贈太師，追封北平王，謚曰莊肅。

translations.literal: In the ninth month of the first year of Guanghua he died, age sixty-three; posthumously enfeoffed as Grand Preceptor of State, posthumously titled Prince of Beiping, posthumous name Zhuangsu.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month of Guanghua year 1 he died, aged sixty-three; he was posthumously enfeoffed as Grand Preceptor of State, posthumously titled Prince of Beiping, with the posthumous name Zhuangsu.

sentences.zh: 子威。

translations.literal: His son Wei.
translations.idiomatic: He had a son named Wei.

sentences.zh: 弘信子 威威，字端己。

translations.literal: Hongxin's son Wei. Wei, courtesy name Duanji.
translations.idiomatic: Hongxin's son Wei, courtesy name Duanji.

sentences.zh: 文德初，授左散騎常侍，充天雄軍節度副使。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Wende he was given Left Regular Attendant and made deputy military commissioner of the Tianxiong Army.
translations.idiomatic: At the start of Wende he received Left Regular Attendant and served as deputy commissioner of the Tianxiong Army.

sentences.zh: 自龍紀至乾寧，十年之中，累加官爵。

translations.literal: From Longji to Qianning, within ten years he was promoted repeatedly in office and enfeoffment.
translations.idiomatic: From Longji through Qianning, over ten years his offices and titles mounted steadily.

sentences.zh: 弘信卒，襲父位爲留後，朝廷從而命之。

translations.literal: When Hongxin died he inherited his father's position as acting commander; the court thereupon confirmed him.
translations.idiomatic: When Hongxin died, Wei inherited the acting command; the court confirmed him.

sentences.zh: 天復末，累加至檢校太傅、兼侍中、長沙王。

translations.literal: At the end of Tianfu he was promoted repeatedly to Honorary Grand Tutor of State, Concurrent Palace Attendant, and Prince of Changsha.
translations.idiomatic: At the end of Tianfu he was promoted repeatedly to honorary Grand Tutor of State, concurrent Palace Attendant, and Prince of Changsha.

sentences.zh: 天祐初，授檢校太尉、守侍中，進封鄴王，賜號「忠勤宣力致理功臣」。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Tianyou he was given Honorary Grand Preceptor of State, Defender Palace Attendant, advanced to Prince of Ye, and granted the title "Meritorious Minister Diligent in Loyal Service and Effective in Governance."
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Tianyou he was given honorary Grand Preceptor of State, defender Palace Attendant, advanced to Prince of Ye, and granted the title Meritorious Minister Diligent in Loyal Service and Effective in Governance.

sentences.zh: 魏之牙中軍者，自至德中，田承嗣盜據相、魏、澶、博、衞、貝等六州，召募軍中子弟置之部下，遂以爲號。

translations.literal: Wei's yamen army — from the Zhide era Tian Chengsi seized by force Xiang, Wei, Chan, Bo, Wei, and Bei prefectures and recruited sons of soldiers in the army to place under his command; thereby they took their name.
translations.idiomatic: Wei's yamen army: since Zhide, when Tian Chengsi seized Xiang, Wei, Chan, Bo, Wei, and Bei, he enrolled soldiers' sons in his command — and that became their name.

sentences.zh: 皆豐給厚賜，不勝驕寵。

translations.literal: All were richly supplied and generously rewarded, beyond bearing in pride and favor.
translations.idiomatic: They were richly paid and heavily favored, grown insufferably proud.

sentences.zh: 年代浸遠，父子相襲，親黨膠固。

translations.literal: As years gradually lengthened, father and son succeeded one another and kin cliques bonded fast.
translations.idiomatic: As time passed, fathers and sons succeeded one another and kin networks hardened.

sentences.zh: 其凶戾者，強買豪奪，逾法犯令，長吏不能禁。

translations.literal: Those who were fierce and cruel forcibly bought and seized by force, transgressed law and violated orders, and senior officials could not restrain them.
translations.idiomatic: Those who were fierce and cruel forcibly bought and plundered, transgressed law and violated orders, and senior officials could not restrain them.

sentences.zh: 變易主帥，有同兒戲，如史憲誠、何進滔、韓君雄、樂彥禎，皆爲其所立。

translations.literal: Changing commanders was like child's play; men such as Shi Xiancheng, He Jintao, Han Junxiong, and Li Yanzhen were all established by them.
translations.idiomatic: Replacing commanders was child's play; Shi Xiancheng, He Jintao, Han Junxiong, and Li Yanzhen were all put up by them.

sentences.zh: 優獎小不如意，則舉族被害。

translations.literal: If favor and reward fell slightly short they would destroy the whole clan.
translations.idiomatic: If rewards fell short even slightly, whole clans were destroyed.

sentences.zh: 威懲其往弊，雖以貨賂姑息，而心銜之。

translations.literal: Wei punished their past abuses; though he placated them with bribes he harbored resentment in his heart.
translations.idiomatic: Wei meant to end their old abuses; though he bought them off, he nursed hatred in his heart.

sentences.zh: 威嗣世之明年，正月，幽州劉仁恭擁兵十萬，謀亂河朔，進陷貝州，長驅攻魏。

translations.literal: In the second year after Wei succeeded to his line, in the first month Liu Rengong of Youzhou gathered a hundred thousand troops, plotted disorder in Hebei, advanced and took Bei prefecture, and drove straight to attack Wei.
translations.idiomatic: The year after Wei succeeded, in the first month Liu Rengong of Youzhou mustered a hundred thousand men, plotted to overturn Hebei, took Bei, and drove on Wei.

sentences.zh: 威求援於汴。

translations.literal: Wei sought aid from Bian.
translations.idiomatic: Wei asked Bian for help.

sentences.zh: 朱全忠遣將李思安屯於洹水。

translations.literal: Zhu Quanzhong sent the general Li Si'an to encamp at the Huan River.
translations.idiomatic: Quanzhong sent Li Si'an to camp on the Huan River.

sentences.zh: 葛從周自邢、洺引軍入魏。

translations.literal: Ge Congzhou from Xing and Ming led troops into Wei.
translations.idiomatic: Ge Congzhou led troops in from Xing and Ming.

sentences.zh: 燕將劉守文、單可及攻汴軍於內黃。

translations.literal: The Yan generals Liu Shouwen and Shan Keji attacked the Bian army at Neihuang.
translations.idiomatic: The Yan generals Liu Shouwen and Shan Keji attacked the Bian army at Neihuang.

sentences.zh: 思安逆戰，大敗之，乘勝追躡。

translations.literal: Si'an met them in battle and inflicted a great defeat, then pressed the pursuit in victory.
translations.idiomatic: Si'an met them, won a great victory, and pursued hotly.

sentences.zh: 從周出會掩擊，覆敗燕軍，斬首三萬。

translations.literal: Congzhou came out to join in a converging strike and utterly defeated the Yan army, beheading thirty thousand.
translations.idiomatic: Congzhou joined the attack from another angle and crushed the Yan army, taking thirty thousand heads.

sentences.zh: 三年，威引汴軍攻滄州以報之。

translations.literal: In the third year Wei led the Bian army to attack Cangzhou in retaliation.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year Wei led Bian troops against Cangzhou in revenge.

sentences.zh: 自是，威感全忠援助之恩，合從景附。

translations.literal: From this time Wei felt gratitude for Quanzhong's aid and attached himself to him in alliance.
translations.idiomatic: From then on Wei was grateful for Quanzhong's help and clung to his alliance.

sentences.zh: 天祐二年七月十三日夜，牙軍裨校李公佺作亂，威僅以身免。

translations.literal: On the night of the thirteenth day of the seventh month of the second year of Tianyou the yamen army staff officer Li Gongxian made disorder; Wei barely escaped with his life.
translations.idiomatic: On the night of the thirteenth day of the seventh month of Tianyou year 2 the yamen army staff officer Li Gongxian made disorder; Wei barely escaped with his life.

sentences.zh: 公佺出奔滄州。

translations.literal: Gongxian fled to Cangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Gongxian fled to Cangzhou.

sentences.zh: 自是愈懼，遣使求援於全忠，密謀破之。

translations.literal: From this he grew ever more afraid and sent envoys to seek aid from Quanzhong, secretly plotting to destroy them.
translations.idiomatic: Wei grew still more afraid, sent envoys to Quanzhong for aid, and secretly plotted to break the yamen army.

sentences.zh: 全忠遣李思安會魏博軍，再攻滄州。

translations.literal: Quanzhong sent Li Si'an to join the Weibo army in again attacking Cangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Quanzhong sent Li Si'an to join the Weibo army in a second attack on Cangzhou.

sentences.zh: 全忠女妻威子廷規，先是卒。

translations.literal: Quanzhong's daughter had married Wei's son Tinggui; she had died earlier.
translations.idiomatic: Quanzhong's daughter had married Wei's son Tinggui and had already died.

sentences.zh: 全忠遣長直軍校馬嗣勳選兵千人，密於輿中實兵甲入魏，言助女葬事。

translations.literal: Quanzhong sent the long-service army officer Ma Sixun to select a thousand troops and secretly fill carriages with armor and weapons to enter Wei, saying it was to assist with the daughter's funeral.
translations.idiomatic: Quanzhong sent Ma Sixun to pick a thousand men and hide arms in funeral carts entering Wei, claiming he came to help bury his daughter.

sentences.zh: 三年正月五日，嗣勳至，全忠親率大軍濟河，言視行營於滄景。

translations.literal: On the fifth day of the first month of the third year Sixun arrived; Quanzhong personally led a great army across the river, saying he was going to inspect the camp at Cangjing.
translations.idiomatic: On the fifth day of the first month of the third year Sixun arrived; Quanzhong crossed the river at the head of a great host, saying he would inspect the Cangjing front.

sentences.zh: 威欲因而出迎，至期，即假全忠帳下銳卒入而夾攻之。

translations.literal: Wei wished thereby to go out to welcome him; when the day came he would borrow Quanzhong's sharp troops from under his tent to enter and strike from both sides.
translations.idiomatic: Wei planned to go out and welcome him, then borrow Quanzhong's picked troops for a pincer strike.

sentences.zh: 牙軍頗疑，堅請不出。

translations.literal: The yamen army was quite suspicious and firmly begged him not to go out.
translations.idiomatic: The yamen troops were suspicious and begged him firmly not to leave the city.

sentences.zh: 威恐洩其事，慰納之。

translations.literal: Wei feared the matter would leak and comforted and accepted them.
translations.idiomatic: Fearing a leak, Wei soothed them and agreed.

sentences.zh: 是月十四日夜，率廝養百十輩，與嗣勳合攻之。

translations.literal: On the night of the fourteenth day of that month he led a hundred-odd personal attendants and joined with Sixun in a combined attack.
translations.idiomatic: On the fourteenth night of that month he led a hundred-odd attendants and joined Sixun in the assault.

sentences.zh: 時宿於牙城者千人，遲明殺之殆盡；

translations.literal: At that time a thousand were quartered in the yamen city; by dawn they were nearly all killed.
translations.idiomatic: A thousand yamen troops were billeted in the inner city; by dawn nearly all were killed.

sentences.zh: 凡八千家，皆破其族。

translations.literal: In all eight thousand households had their clans destroyed.
translations.idiomatic: Eight thousand households in all had their lineages wiped out.

sentences.zh: 魏軍攻滄州者，在歷亭聞有變，其將史仁遇擁之，保於高唐。

translations.literal: The Wei troops attacking Cangzhou were at Liting; when they heard of the change their commander Shi Renyu rallied them and held Gaotang.
translations.idiomatic: The Wei force besieging Cangzhou was at Liting; hearing of the upheaval, Shi Renyu rallied them and held Gaotang.

sentences.zh: 六州之內，皆爲讎敵，累月平之。

translations.literal: Within the six prefectures all became enemies; it took months to pacify them.
translations.idiomatic: Throughout the six prefectures everyone became an enemy; pacification took months.

sentences.zh: 威仕梁數年後卒，年三十四，位至守太師、兼中書令，贈尚書令，謚曰貞壯。

translations.literal: Wei served Liang for several years and then died, age thirty-four, reaching Defender Grand Preceptor of State and Concurrent Director of the Department of State Affairs; posthumously given Minister of the Imperial Secretariat, posthumous name Zhenzhuang.
translations.idiomatic: Wei served Liang for several years and then died, aged thirty-four, reaching defender Grand Preceptor of State and concurrent Director of the Department of State Affairs; he was posthumously given Minister of the Imperial Secretariat, with the posthumous name Zhenzhuang.

sentences.zh: 威性明敏，達於吏道。

translations.literal: Wei by nature was bright and keen and understood the ways of administration.
translations.idiomatic: Wei was quick-witted and skilled in administration.

sentences.zh: 伏膺儒術，招納文人，聚書至萬卷。

translations.literal: He devoted himself to Confucian learning, recruited literary men, and gathered books to ten thousand scrolls.
translations.idiomatic: He honored Confucian learning, gathered literati, and amassed ten thousand scrolls.

sentences.zh: 每花朝月夕，與賓佐賦詠，甚有情致。

translations.literal: Every flower festival and moonlit evening he composed and chanted poetry with his guests and staff, with much charm and feeling.
translations.idiomatic: On every flower festival and moonlit evening he composed and recited poetry with his guests and staff, with much grace and feeling.

sentences.zh: 錢塘人羅隱者，有當世詩名，自號「江東生」。

translations.literal: There was Luo Yin of Qiantang, who had a contemporary reputation in poetry and styled himself "The Man of Jiangdong."
translations.idiomatic: There was Luo Yin of Qiantang, who enjoyed a contemporary reputation in poetry and styled himself the Man of Jiangdong.

sentences.zh: 威遣使賂遺，敘其宗姓，推爲叔父。

translations.literal: Wei sent envoys with gifts, narrated their shared clan surname, and promoted him as paternal uncle.
translations.idiomatic: Wei sent envoys with gifts, claimed kinship through their clan name, and honored him as uncle.

sentences.zh: 隱亦集其詩寄之。

translations.literal: Yin also collected his poems and mailed them to him.
translations.idiomatic: Yin in turn assembled his own poems and sent them as a gift.

sentences.zh: 威酷嗜其作，目己所爲曰《偷江東集》，凡五卷，今鄴中人士諷詠之。

translations.literal: Wei was passionately fond of his writings and called his own compositions The Collection Stolen from Jiangdong, five scrolls in all; the gentlemen of Ye still chant them today.
translations.idiomatic: Wei adored his poetry, called his own work The Collection Stolen from Jiangdong in five scrolls, and men of Ye still recite it.

sentences.zh: 史臣曰史臣曰：魏、鎮、燕三鎮，不能制之也久矣。

translations.literal: The historian says: The historian says: Wei, Zhen, and Yan — the three commands — the court has long been unable to control them.
translations.idiomatic: The historian writes: For the three commands of Wei, Zhen, and Yan, the court has long since lost the power to control them.

sentences.zh: 兵強地廣，合從連衡。

translations.literal: Their armies are strong and their territories broad; they ally and counter-alliance.
translations.idiomatic: Their armies are strong and their territories broad; they form alliances and counter-alliances.

sentences.zh: 爵命雖假於朝廷，群臣自謀於元帥。

translations.literal: Though titles and commissions are borrowed from the court, the ministers plot for themselves under the military commander.
translations.idiomatic: Titles came from the court, but the ministers schemed under the commander's banner.

sentences.zh: 如史憲誠等五家，其初皆因此而得之，其後亦因此而失之。

translations.literal: Men such as the five houses of Shi Xiancheng — at first they all gained power thereby, and afterward they also lost power thereby.
translations.idiomatic: The five houses such as Shi Xiancheng first rose this way — and later fell the same way.

sentences.zh: 蓋不知取之以權，守之以仁，則遠矣。

translations.literal: For they did not know how to take power by expedient means and hold it with benevolence — how far they were from that!
translations.idiomatic: They did not know to seize power by expedience and keep it through benevolence; how far they were from wisdom.

sentences.zh: 若善繼者，史氏、羅氏之二子有焉，其餘不足觀也。

translations.literal: As for those who succeeded well, the two sons of the Shi and Luo clans had it; the rest are not worth viewing.
translations.idiomatic: Only the Shi and Luo heirs truly carried on well; the rest are hardly worth notice.

sentences.zh: 贊贊曰：逆取順守，古亦有之。

translations.literal: Praise says: Praise says: To take by rebellion and guard by compliance — the ancients too had such cases.
translations.idiomatic: The encomium says: Seizing power through rebellion yet ruling with obedience to the court — even the ancients knew such cases.

sentences.zh: 如其逆守，滅亡必隨。

translations.literal: If one holds by rebellion, destruction and extinction must follow.
translations.idiomatic: Hold power through rebellion, and ruin follows inevitably.

sentences.zh: 史、何、韓、樂，世數盛衰。

translations.literal: Shi, He, Han, and Le — generations rise and fall.
translations.idiomatic: Shi, He, Han, and Le — their houses rose and fell with the generations.

sentences.zh: 足以爲鑒，念茲在茲。

translations.literal: They are enough to serve as a mirror; let this be kept in mind.
translations.idiomatic: They are warning enough; keep this lesson close.
